question.prompt: The region consisting of all points in three-dimensional space within \(3\) units of line segment \(AB\) has volume \(216\pi.\) What is the length \(AB?\)

solutions.title: Separate the cylinder and end caps
solutions.explanation:
The key is to separate points nearest the interior of \(AB\) from points nearest its endpoints. Let \(h=AB\), and consider the two planes through \(A\) and \(B\) perpendicular to \(AB\).

Between these planes, the points within distance \(3\) of the segment form a cylinder of radius \(3\) and height \(h\). Beyond either plane, the nearest point of the segment is the corresponding endpoint, giving an outward hemisphere of radius \(3\).

The two hemispheres together have the volume of one sphere. Adding the volumes gives
\[
216\pi=\pi(3)^2h+\frac{4}{3}\pi(3)^3
=9\pi h+36\pi.
\]
Therefore
\[
h=\frac{216-36}{9}=20.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{AB=20}\) units, choice \(\text{D}\).
